Definition: from G4862 and a derivative of G2244; a co-aged person, i.e. alike in years:--equal.
BiblicalUsage: Paul says he profited in the Jews' religion above many his equals in his own nation, being more exceedingly zealous for the traditions of his fathers. He was ahead of his own generation, and the very zeal that made him first among his equals is what he had to leave behind to follow Christ.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe zeal without Christ only carries me further wrong, and I hold that being first among my equals is worth nothing beside knowing Him.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
